subject: treehouse

I'm planning out a stylized three.js treehouse scene built from primitives—trunk, branches, canopy, platform, walls, roof, window, ladder, and extra details like a rope bridge, lantern, and flags—sized realistically at around 8 meters tall and using a seeded RNG for leaf placement and canvas textures for surface detail.

For the treehouse platform I'm working out its position and size relative to the trunk so the deck hugs the trunk without an awkward hole, deciding to let the platform slightly overlap the trunk rather than cutting a notch, and adjusting the z-offset so the deck clears the trunk's radius at that height.

Finally I'm laying out the cabin walls on the platform—back wall, two side walls with window openings, and a front wall split for a doorway—plus plank-line details for texture.

Working out the roof slab rotations so each slope rises correctly toward the ridge, then adding gable-end triangles for the front and back walls.

I'm also considering adding a rope bridge connecting the treehouse platform to a second smaller tree nearby.

For the bridge I'll build a second trunk and platform, then sag a dozen small plank boxes along a quadratic curve between the two platforms with thin cylinder rails, rotating each plank to match the slope. I'm also sketching a hanging lantern bracket near the front roof eave, deciding on the best corner and position for it.

For the ladder, I'm positioning it leaning against the front-left side of the platform, running from a ground point up to near the deck edge, computing the rail orientation with a quaternion rotation from the Y axis, and adding perpendicular rungs using a reusable segment helper function.
